research_rationale:
Executive Order 13611 of 2012-05-16 (77 FR 29533, PDF pages 1-3) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 22 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to Yemen declared in the lead clause of Executive Order 13611 on May 16, 2012. Notice of May 7, 2026 (Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 90, May 11, 2026; FR Doc. 2026-09385) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond May 16, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only: the Notice of May 9, 2022 and an entry labelled Proc. 11026, May 5, 2026, discussed below. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. The Federal Register index of order notes labels a cross-reference to Proc. 11026 of May 5, 2026; its text is not held in the repository and the entry is a See reference, not a revoked-by or superseded-by note. The Notice of May 7, 2026, issued two days later, states that the Yemen emergency declared in this order must continue in effect beyond May 16, 2026, which is inconsistent with any ending of the order by that proclamation. Savings: none arises because the order remained in force at the cutoff.
